answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The horizon multiplier is published, charged in hollow, and karst lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3257 identities would post 3387 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
